setups.name: Model Knows
setups.why: We and Vegas pick different winners and our line has our team by 2+ points: back our team on the moneyline (judge it by the price just before tip, once lineups are in)
setups.note: 2020-21..2025-26 at the closing price: our team won 136-102 (57.1%) outright, +25% per bet on the moneyline; covered 145-91 (61.4%). The backtest knew who played, so judge it near tip

setups.name: Combo watch
setups.why: One model weighing about 40 things we know by 11am (rest and travel, the standings, recent form and pace, our ratings, the line and how it has moved) flags the side it's most sure of; about 1 game in 20 qualifies
setups.note: Most confident 5% of games, walk-forward: 140-104 (57.4%), 36-25 in the 2025-26 exam

setups.name: Tired Traveler
setups.why: Away team on the 2nd night of a back-to-back AND it crossed a time zone since its last game (home team rested): bet the home team
setups.note: 178-143 (55.5%) at the morning line 2020-21..2025-26, every season 51%+

setups.name: Vegas Knows
setups.why: Our line has the game within 4 points but Vegas has the favorite 3+ points bigger than we do: Vegas likely knows something we don't (injuries, lineups, a new roster). A moneyline read: the Vegas favorite usually wins, but at its price that isn't a bet. Don't bet against it
setups.note: Moneyline only. 2020-21..2025-26: the Vegas favorite won 375-231 (61.9%) outright. Its typical price is -230, which needs about 70% to break even, so betting it lost about 11% per bet (it covered the spread only 45%). Information, not a pick: it tells you not to bet against the favorite
